page.text: Web Summit 2026 is bringing the world to Lisbon, with 70,003 attendees from 164 countries, making this its most international edition yet. The event has also broken its investor attendance record for the second consecutive year, welcoming 1,943 investors. The tickets to the 2026 edition of Web Summit, in Lisbon, sold out last week, closing at 70,003 following strong demand for exhibition space from partners. More than 10,000 startups will attend Web Summit, while the sold-out exhibition floor will feature 3,052 companies from 110 countries, alongside major partners from some of the world’s largest technology giants, Apple, Meta, Google, and Intel. Windows into the world Web Summit has always been a window into the future, and that future is being built in countries outside of the United States. Governments from Brazil, China, Qatar, Poland, Hungary, Lithuania, Slovenia, South Korea, and more are sending trade delegations to promote their domestic tech talent and expand global trade links. “Welcome to the most global Web Summit ever. We are joined by attendees from 164 countries, more than ever before”, said Web Summit founder and CEO Paddy Cosgrave at Opening Night. “Brazil, like every country in the global south, continues to grow its presence here and that growth is reflected in this Web Summit… more startups are coming from São Paulo than Paris.” “This year has, without a doubt, the most important lineup of technology speakers we ever had. And they are all from China. Because Chinese companies are building more of our shared Future than companies from anywhere else. And we should open our eyes to that future”, continued Web Summit founder and CEO Paddy Cosgrave. Web Summit 2026’s opening night featured dancing humanoid robots from Chinese company AgiBot and flying car technology from Xpeng AeroHT. Speaking on Web Summit’s host country, Web Summit CEO also highlighted the record number of Portuguese startups: “This year we have the largest number of Portuguese startups at Web Summit ever. This speaks to the amazing rise of Portugal over the last 10 years”, said Paddy Cosgrave. Despite a challenging fundraising environment for many early-stage companies in Europe, startups are showing up in force at Web Summit 2026. Portugal and Ireland are seeing record participation, with 350 Portuguese startups and 115 Irish startups, the highest number from Ireland since Web Summit moved to Lisbon. The Web Summit effect on Portugal The impact of hosting Web Summit in Lisbon goes well beyond the four days of the event. A new report by EY found that Web Summit has contributed nearly €2.5 billion to the Portuguese economy over the past decade, around €250 million a year. The report also highlighted the lasting benefits for Portuguese startups exhibiting at the event, which were more likely to grow their revenue and create jobs. Since Web Summit first came to Lisbon in 2016, the number of Portuguese startups has doubled, while their combined annual turnover has grown from €1.23 billion to €2.85 billion. Record number of investors The record investor turnout includes Accel, Bessemer Venture Partners, BlackRock, TPG, Union Square Ventures, Index Ventures, Amino Capital, Atomico, the Qatar Investment Authority and Tencent. New data from PitchBook highlights the global reach of investors attending Web Summit 2026. Investors attending Web Summit have participated in 60% of global VC deal value and 73% of US VC deal value in 2026, based on data through September 30. China shares glimpse into the future China’s growing influence in AI and robotics will be a major theme at Web Summit 2026, which brings together 960 speakers from around the world, including tech leaders from China, Europe and the US. The event will welcome its largest-ever Chinese delegation, with speakers including Unitree, one of China’s leading humanoid robotics companies, represented by co-founder Li Chen ; Tencent’s chief investment and strategy officer (EMEA) Ling Ge ; Xiaomi CM

page.text: The Government of Portugal has formally advised Web Summit that, due to the risks posed by Storm Charles, including tidal flooding, severe disruption to public transport and the impact of high winds on external structures, Day 2 of Web Summit should not take place. This follows discussions with the Portuguese Government, the National Emergency and Civil Protection Authority (ANEPC), and the Public Security Police (PSP). Web Summit will of course respect the Government’s direction, and accordingly, Day 2 (Wednesday, November 11th) will not take place. The safety and security of our attendees, staff and contractors is always our absolute priority. Web Summit aims to proceed with Day 3 (Thursday, November 12) as planned, following the passing of Storm Charles. We will continue to work closely with the relevant authorities and emergency services, monitor conditions and provide further updates as soon as confirmed information becomes available. Web Summit will communicate directly with those impacted.

page.text: Web Summit 2025 is welcoming 71,386 attendees this week, including CEOs, government and trade delegations, global media, and more startups and investors than ever before. Below we present Web Summit 2025, by the numbers: Key takeaways Web Summit 2025 joins 71,386 attendees from 157 countries. 1,857 investors are joining Web Summit 2025 from 86 countries, a 74% surge from last year’s 1,066. It is the largest number ever to attend the event. 2,725 startups, from 108 countries, will be exhibiting, with AI and machine learning emerging as the top industry. Notably, 40% of startups are women-founded. ⁠⁠Nearly 200 startups raised funding post-event: According to Crunchbase, nearly 200 startups from Web Summit’s 2024 Startup Programme secured post-event investment, with total funding reaching $715.5 million. You can read more about it here . 869 speakers join Web Summit’s stages this year , with Opening Night featuring leaders shaping the future of tech, business and culture, including the most followed person on TikTok Khaby Lame; Lovable, Co-founder and CEO Anton Osika; entrepreneur and tennis legend Maria Sharapova. 1,519 publishers, CEOs, editors and reporters, from outlets including The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, CNBC, The Economist, Der Spiegel, Le Monde, Axios, CGTN, Globo, Sapo, Renascença, Valor Económico, RTP and Euronews are joining Web Summit to explore new technologies and ideas shaping the future. 268 government delegation s are joining from 82 countries, including Portugal, Spain, Poland, Brazil, Angola, Germany, the US, Canada, Ireland, Austria, Japan, China, Belgium, India, Mexico, Qatar, Australia, and more. 400 curated meetups are underway , helping attendees make meaningful connections, from women in tech and backend developers to ai innovators, to a giant Jenga session. Partners exhibiting at Web Summit include IBM, Visa, Qualcomm, Alibaba Cloud, Revolut People, KPMG, Replit, Huawei, and LinkedIn. Ten years ago it already felt like the world was changing fast, but it’s nothing compared to how fast the world is changing today , said Web Summit CEO Paddy Cosgrave on Web Summit’s Opening Night. It’s been 10 years since a tiny three person startup called Revolut showed up at Web Summit. Today Revolut is Europe’s most valuable private tech company.” “I’ve no doubt that there’s another Revolut at Web Summit, maybe several. Two or three people with a tiny stand and a huge idea. I hope you all take the opportunity to meet our more than 2,500 startups who are exhibiting over the coming three days , he continued. More investors than ever A record 1,857 investors are set to attend Web Summit 2025, the highest in the event’s history and a 74% surge from last year’s 1,066. The growth underscores the global appetite for meaningful connections and in-person deal-making at an event that will showcase the ideas from 2,725 startups from 108 countries. This year’s investor community includes partners from some of the most influential funds in venture capital, including QED Investors, Accel, Amino and Indico. AI emerges as the most represented industry A record 2,725 startups from 108 countries will exhibit on the show floor, with AI and machine learning emerging as the top industry, representing nearly one-fifth of all exhibiting startups. SaaS, healthtech and wellness, fintech, and sustainability complete the top five sectors. Notably, 40% of startups are women-founded , in line with Web Summit’s efforts to increase visibility for women across the global tech ecosystem. 869 speakers will be discussing the future of tech Toto Wolff, Team Principal, CEO & Co-owner of Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team; Maria Sharapova, tennis champion and entrepreneur; Alex Schultz, Chief Marketing Officer at Meta, and Cristiano Amon President & CEO of Qualcomm, a global leader in wireless technology and semiconductors are amongst the leaders in technology, business, sports and entertainment that will be taking to the stage to disc
